partners.mechanism_chain: APOA2 (HGNC:547) —DISRUPTS→ Apolipoprotein A-II deficiency (MONDO:0980749); MED12 (HGNC:7090) —DISRUPTS→ Transcriptional regulation (GO:0006355); Transcriptional regulation (GO:0006355) —LEADS_TO→ X-linked intellectual disability, spondylometaphyseal dysplasia, and related disorders (MONDO:0010477). Mutations in APOA2 directly cause apolipoprotein A-II deficiency. MED12, a component of the Mediator complex, regulates transcription. Disruption of MED12 function, potentially through loss-of-function mechanisms, leads to a spectrum of developmental disorders including X-linked intellectual disability and spondylometaphyseal dysplasia. The shared underlying mechanism is the disruption of normal cellular processes due to genetic defects in genes that are critical for cellular function, with APOA2 being directly involved in lipid metabolism and MED12 in broader transcriptional regulation, both contributing to distinct but potentially overlapping disease modules.

#### 1. cholestasis-pigmentary retinopathy-cleft palate syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.785)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:11957)

**Proposed mechanism:** MED12 (HGNC:7101) —DISRUPTS→ Transcription regulation by Mediator Complex (GO:0000977); Transcription regulation by Mediator Complex (GO:0000977) —LEADS_TO→ Intrahepatic cholestasis (HP:0003178); Transcription regulation by Mediator Complex (GO:0000977) —LEADS_TO→ Pigmentary retinopathy (HP:0000548); Transcription regulation by Mediator Complex (GO:0000977) —LEADS_TO→ Cleft palate (HP:0000175). Haploinsufficiency of MED12 disrupts the normal function of the Mediator Complex, a key transcriptional coactivator. This disruption leads to aberrant gene expression, manifesting as intrahepatic cholestasis in MONDO:0010477, and pigmentary retinopathy and cleft palate in cholestasis-pigmentary retinopathy-cleft palate syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of pathogenic variants in MED12 in individuals with either MONDO:0010477 or cholestasis-pigmentary retinopathy-cleft palate syndrome, or the identification of distinct causal genes for each disease. _(variant: A common, benign variant in MED12 with a frequency >1% in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the role of MED12 haploinsufficiency in these distinct yet mechanistically linked diseases could pave the way for targeted therapies aimed at modulating transcriptional activity or compensating for the disrupted Mediator Complex function.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of functionally distinct pathogenic variants in MED12 for each disease, one causing haploinsufficiency for intellectual disability and another causing haploinsufficiency for marfanoid habitus, without affecting the other phenotype. _(variant: gnomad_v3.1.2:chrX:100509198-100509198-G-A)_
